one_liner: Rust-based JavaScript/TypeScript linter and toolchain that replaces ESLint with 50-100x faster linting.
what_it_does: Oxc is a Rust toolchain for JavaScript/TypeScript (parser, transformer, minifier, resolver) that also ships Oxlint, a standalone linter meant to replace ESLint. Oxlint runs via `npx oxlint` or a native CLI binary, reads an ESLint-like flat config (.oxlintrc.json), and reports comparable diagnostics, but it is not an ESLint plugin host: its own JS-plugin system bridges only some ESLint plugins, and local custom ESLint plugins do not carry over automatically. Type-aware TypeScript rules require a separate component, oxlint-tsgolint, built on TypeScript 7.
how_it_is_fast: Oxlint reuses oxc's own parser and semantic analyzer, built on an arena allocator (oxc_allocator), so most rules run in a single AST traversal instead of ESLint's per-rule/per-plugin dispatch. Files are linted in parallel across CPU cores via Rayon, with the `ignore` crate (SIMD-accelerated) walking the file tree, so throughput scales with core count. That parallelism is why the gap widens on more cores: ~17x single-threaded vs ESLint, up to ~62-118x multi-threaded on 8-12 core machines in the project's own benchmark.
when_to_use: Large JS/TS monorepos where ESLint's per-file startup and plugin dispatch overhead dominates CI time
Standard-rule linting (no exotic plugin needs) where raw throughput matters more than full rule-set parity
Multi-core CI runners or dev machines, since the speedup scales with thread count
Teams migrating incrementally, running Oxlint alongside ESLint to cover the remaining rule gap
Projects wanting near-instant `npx oxlint` feedback with zero required config
when_not_to_use: Codebases that depend on ESLint plugins with no Oxlint equivalent or JS-plugin bridge
Projects needing full type-aware linting parity with typescript-eslint - gain drops to 8-12x and rule coverage is narrower, and it needs the separate oxlint-tsgolint/TypeScript 7 component
Repos still on legacy ESLint v8 config - must convert to flat config via @eslint/migrate-config before the official migration tool works
Setups with local/custom ESLint plugins - these do not migrate automatically
Single-core or low-core environments, where the advantage shrinks toward the ~17x single-threaded figure

integration.dependencies: Rust workspace of internal oxc_* crates (oxc_allocator, oxc_parser, oxc_linter, oxc_semantic, ...) plus rayon, bpaf, napi, tower-lsp-server; npm CLI package ships a prebuilt native binary with no user-facing JS deps
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.96.0 (workspace MSRV, N-2 policy), edition 2024; no Rust toolchain needed to use the prebuilt npm binary
integration.platforms: Linux (glibc/musl; x86-64, arm/aarch64, riscv64, powerpc64le), macOS (x86-64, arm64), Windows (x86-64, i686, arm64), plus wasm and OpenHarmony targets per the npm package's optionalDependencies
integration.thread_safety: not documented for the Rust crates as an embeddable library API; the CLI itself parallelizes file processing across threads via Rayon (thread count configurable, e.g. --threads=1 for single-threaded runs)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: reads ESLint's flat config format and reports similar diagnostics, but implements a subset of ESLint's rules with a different plugin architecture, and needs the separate oxlint-tsgolint component for type-aware TS rules

gotchas: Legacy ESLint v8 configs must be converted to flat config first (via @eslint/migrate-config) before the @oxlint/migrate tool works
Local/custom ESLint plugins don't migrate automatically and need manual setup
Type-aware rules require the separate oxlint-tsgolint binary, which depends on TypeScript 7
The published Oxlint-vs-Biome benchmark enables only a single rule (no-debugger) on both linters, so the ~2x figure isn't representative of full rule-set performance
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Over Biome specifically: the same VS Code benchmark run by the Oxc project shows Oxlint 2.5-3.3x faster (though that test used only the no-debugger rule, so treat it as a floor, not a full-ruleset comparison). The other catalogued siblings (Ruff, Pyrefly, ty, clangd-tidy) target Python or C++, so within JS/TS linting Oxlint is the only ESLint-throughput entry here besides Biome.
verified_claims_summary: Oxc's own bench-linter repo (hyperfine, 1 warmup, non-zero exits ignored, ESLint v9, no ESLint cache) measured Oxlint linting the VS Code source tree at 62.10x/118.25x/60.09x ESLint's speed on an M2 Max 12-core / M4 Max / M3 Air 8-core respectively, and ~17x single-threaded (31.025s vs 1.824s on M2 Max); vs Biome on the same tree with only the no-debugger rule enabled, 2.72x/2.49x/3.31x across the same three machines; vs typescript-eslint with type-aware rules on Vue core and Sentry (M2 Max), 8.22x and 12.38x respectively.
status_note: Actively maintained (commits as recent as today, 22.9k stars across the oxc monorepo) with VoidZero backing; MIT licensed and directly usable via `npx oxlint`, though ESLint rule/plugin parity is still incomplete.
